messages:
alex: quick question — we're seeing a reproducible stall in the Python streaming client when the server splits a UTF-8 emoji across chunks. the readloop pauses ~200ms then resumes, which triggers slowconsumer backpressure on our event loop. stack: python3.11, aiohttp, custom incremental parser. anyone seen this?

jia: hmm — sounds like a decode boundary issue. are you doing incremental decoding with a decoder that preserves incomplete multibyte chars? e.g. codecs.getincrementaldecoder('utf-8')()

alex: currently we do data.decode('utf-8') on each chunk then append to a unicode buffer; that might be the culprit.

sam: yep that's the classic bug. utf-8 sequences can split across chunks. either use an incremental decoder or keep bytes and let a decoder handle split sequences. quick example: 

```py
import codecs, json
dec = codecs.getincrementaldecoder('utf-8')()
buf = ''
for chunk in stream:
    # chunk is bytes
    buf += dec.decode(chunk)
    while True:
        try:
            obj, idx = json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode(buf)
            handle(obj)
            buf = buf[idx:].lstrip()
        except ValueError:
            break
```

sam: also consider using ijson or a C-backed streaming parser if you need low-latency parsing.

jia: if you control the server, ndjson (newline-delimited JSON) avoids this problem entirely and simplifies streaming.

alex: thanks, i'll try switching to incremental decoder. we also see backpressure: when parse can't keep up, the client readloop stalls and aiohttp pauses reads. what's the recommended approach to avoid large stalls?

sam: two main levers: (1) speed up parsing (C libs) (2) decouple read vs parse. put raw bytes into a bounded asyncio.Queue and have worker(s) parse from it. that way you control backpressure by queue maxsize and can choose to drop/slow readers before buffering grows.

devex-bot: PR 9876 added a streaming helper for python incremental decoding: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/9876 :eyes:

jia: @alex FYI the SDK now has config options streaming_buffer_size and parse_worker_count. try streaming_buffer_size=8, parse_worker_count=1 as a starting point.

alex: i'll open a tiny repro and link it here. quick question: is it safe to keep reading from aiohttp while parse workers are busy?

sam: safe if you use a bounded queue. if you unbounded-read, OS buffers + aiohttp can accumulate and risk OOM. use asyncio.Queue(maxsize=N) and await queue.put(chunk) which will naturally apply backpressure to the reader. or use put_nowait with a try/except to drop/throttle.

alex: uploaded gist with minimal repro: https://gist.github.com/example-repro :thumbsup:

jia: looked — small nit: your example recreates the decoder each chunk. keep the incremental decoder instance across the loop so it buffers partial utf-8 sequences. after that it looks good. :+1:

sam: TL;DR: 1) keep an incremental utf-8 decoder, 2) feed bytes into a bounded queue, 3) consider a C parser or ndjson if you control the server.

alex: awesome, thanks everyone — will iterate and post results.
